The handbook's lodgepole pine is the species as cut for timber, mostly the inland variety latifolia; shore pine (var. contorta) is not tested apart.

traits.wood_moisture_green_share.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 4-1, Pine, lodgepole: average moisture content of green wood, heartwood 41% and sapwood 120% of oven-dry mass; stated as a share, the range between them with its middle typical where both are given. traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Pinus contorta (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.4 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 51 records in 8 sources); trunks 0.4, branches 0.44. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.needles_per_fascicle.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 59), Pinus contorta in its shore form: needles in twos, the sheath kept, 3 to 5 cm, dense on the branches, kept two or three years, rarely longer; seed cones ovoid and oblique, 3 to 5 cm (FEIS: 3.8 to 5.1 cm). They open when ripe and then fall soon or hang on for many years, so no retention is stated.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Pinus, table 2, read): seed bearing begins at 4 to 8 years in var. contorta. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 8 years set by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a small, irregular pine with a rounded to flat-topped crown, stout upturned branches and tufts of short, paired needles at the twig ends. Not fitted to measurements. Cones (plant forms F3): 3 to 6 cm, often closed and kept on the tree for years; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spray area (plant roadmap P4): the area its card draws now that its needles stand in fascicles. Spec rework E6d: `cone_length`, `needle_years` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated characters. Conifer form (pinidae revision 5): `branch_reach` fitted so the open-grown crown keeps revision 4's radius at the oldest keyframe, and `pipe_rings` refitted to the dbh references now that the crown holds more foliage; `branch_ageing` is gone with the calendar ageing it set; `epi_chance` 0, as pines seldom sprout from dormant buds on their branches (general knowledge, not measured). Needle shading (generator revision 82): `side_chance` raised from 0.6 to 0.8 so the crown keeps the urban tree database's leaf area per crown area (3.6 to 6.8) now that its needles shade only their true area.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 11 m tall and 30 cm across at breast height at 40 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: yellow-green needles; dark, thick, furrowed bark. Needle shoots (plant roadmap P4): needles in pairs, 3 to 7 cm long and 1 to 2 mm wide, so a needle 0.03 as wide as it is long (`width`), 2 to a fascicle (`bundle`), from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): dark brown bark broken into small blocky plates; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `needle`, `bundle`, `ranks` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated needles.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted variety the name resolves to (the accepted name).
